/how-it-works.title: How Heimdall Works | Lead Targets, Search & Teams
/how-it-works.description: Compare Google Places and Foursquare lead discovery. See how to connect API keys, choose a lead target, review results, and work with your team.
/how-it-works.heading: How Heimdall finds local business leads
sections: Connect your own provider key
Use Google Places for operational businesses without a listed website, or Foursquare to find business websites, phones, and social profiles. Provider fees are separate from ₹100.
Choose a lead target
Choose 10, 25, or 50 leads per search. The target sets an upper bound and actual results depend on the provider, category, and location.
How Google Places expands a search
Heimdall can fetch more pages and try related category and area variations while deduplicating by place ID. Foursquare searches the chosen category and city in a single request.
Follow search progress
Switch between dashboard screens while your search runs. When results are ready, a notification shows the count and opens the results.
Review match quality and permissions
Phone numbers may be duplicated, malformed or unrelated. Public availability is not marketing consent.
Save eligible results and work together

Named files, CSV exports and team copies require permission under source terms and applicable law. Saved files and exports include returned business details; provider permissions remain a launch-review requirement.

/google-places-setup.title: Connect Google Places API to Heimdall | Setup Guide
/google-places-setup.description: Set up Google Cloud billing, enable Places API (New), create and restrict your API key, and connect it to Heimdall. Understand separate Google usage charges.
/google-places-setup.heading: Connect Google Places.
sections: Create your Google Cloud project
Select or create a project in Google Cloud Console and link a billing account.
Enable Places API (New)
Enable Places API (New), create an API key, and restrict it to the required API and your server's outbound IP where appropriate.
Connect your key
Sign in to Heimdall, open Scrape → Google Places, and connect your key. The key stays in your backend session until sign-out or session expiry.
Monitor usage and billing
Google Places usage is billed separately by Google according to your usage. The ₹100 Heimdall purchase does not cover Google Places and Foursquare API fees.
Provider policy review
Google restricts storage and export of Places content. Full-result storage, CSV export and team sharing remain subject to provider review before launch.
Free API requests
Google’s global pricing includes 1,000 free Text Search Enterprise requests each month. India-eligible accounts have separate allowances. Google bills the account linked to your key.

/google-places.title: Google Places Lead Discovery | Heimdall
/google-places.description: Discover operational businesses without a listed website using Google Places. Review available details and choose a lead target with your own API key.
/google-places.heading: Find businesses without listed websites
sections: Start with a business type and city

Enter a query such as restaurants in Boston. Heimdall searches Google Places and keeps operational listings that do not include a website in the returned record. A missing field does not prove the business has no website elsewhere.
Set a realistic target

Choose 10, 25, or 50 unique matches. The search can page through results and try related categories and areas, deduplicating by place ID. It stops at the target, cancellation, provider failure, an internal request limit, or exhausted variations. Results are not guaranteed.
Review before outreach

Check business relevance, location, and available contact details. Public listings are not consent to marketing. Retention, export and team sharing depend on provider permissions; API access alone does not grant those rights.
Bring your own key
Connect a Places API (New) key from your Google Cloud project. Your provider usage is billed separately from Heimdall Premium.

/foursquare.title: Foursquare Business Discovery | Heimdall
/foursquare.description: Find local businesses with Foursquare in Heimdall. Filter available websites, phones and social profiles, using your own Foursquare Places API key.
/foursquare.heading: Discover business contacts with Foursquare
sections: Search a niche and location
Search businesses by category and city. Heimdall requests up to your selected target of 10, 25, or 50 listings in one Foursquare search. Coverage varies by location and category.
Filter the fields you need
Use website, phone, and social filters to focus the returned listings. Not every business includes every field, and a filter can reduce the visible result count.
Review the original business
Open an available website or social profile to confirm relevance before contacting anyone. Contact details are unverified. Follow provider terms and applicable outreach rules.
Control your provider account
Use your own Foursquare Places key. Provider charges and allowances belong to your account and are separate from Heimdall’s price.

/for-freelancers.title: Local Business Leads for Freelancers | Heimdall
/for-freelancers.description: Build a focused local prospect list for your freelance services. Discover businesses, review available details, and organize eligible leads with Heimdall.
/for-freelancers.heading: A focused prospecting workflow for freelancers
sections: Choose one service and one niche
Start with a specific offer, such as website design for independent cafés. Search one city at a time so you can review relevance rather than collecting a broad untargeted list.
Find a reason to reach out

Google Places can identify listings without a website field. Foursquare can surface available websites and social profiles. Check the business yourself; do not assume a missing listing field means it needs your services.
Keep useful context
Where source permissions allow, organize eligible leads in a named folder. Record your own research and next step, then avoid contacting the same business twice.
Make outreach relevant
Use a lawful channel, explain a specific useful idea, and honor opt-outs. Heimdall does not send outreach or guarantee clients.

/for-web-designers.title: Business Discovery for Web Designers | Heimdall
/for-web-designers.description: Find local businesses to research for web design services. Compare Google Places and Foursquare signals and organize a thoughtful prospecting workflow.
/for-web-designers.heading: Research your next web design opportunity
sections: Look beyond the listing
A Google Places record without a website is a research signal. Search the business name separately before concluding it has no site.
Review existing websites

Use Foursquare’s available website field to inspect businesses in your target niche. Evaluate mobile usability, accessibility and clarity yourself; Heimdall does not automatically audit website quality.
Prepare a concrete suggestion
Write a short observation based on what you actually reviewed. Avoid telling a business its site is broken or outdated without evidence.
Track your own progress
Organize eligible results and record notes with your team where permitted. Keep provider data permissions and outreach rules in mind.

/for-agencies.title: Local Business Prospecting for Agencies | Heimdall
/for-agencies.description: Coordinate local business research with your agency team. Discover businesses, organize eligible lead folders, add shared notes and track completion.
/for-agencies.heading: Keep your agency’s prospect research together
sections: Define a clear research brief
Choose a niche, city, and service offer before searching. Agree on what makes a business relevant and which provider fields your team needs.
Compare discovery methods
Use Google Places for operational listings without a website field, or Foursquare for available business websites, phone numbers and social profiles. Both require your own provider key.
Coordinate eligible folders
Create or join a team and import a folder only when source terms allow sharing. Members can add attributed notes and mark leads Done so the team can see progress.
Keep quality checks human
Verify details, assign a next action in notes, and check for duplicate outreach. Heimdall is a research workspace, not an automated outreach or revenue guarantee.

/guides.heading: Learn the local discovery workflow
sections: Connect your provider

Search and review
Use the illustrated walkthrough to understand query entry, lead targets and result filters. The screenshots show the actual interface with illustrative input, not guaranteed search results.
Organize and collaborate

/guides/first-search.title: Your First Business Search in Heimdall | Illustrated Guide
/guides/first-search.description: Follow an illustrated Heimdall search walkthrough: connect a provider key, enter a niche and city, choose a target, and review available results.
/guides/first-search.heading: Run your first business search
sections: 1. Connect your own provider key
Sign in, open Scrape, and choose Google Places or Foursquare. Connect the appropriate key. Never include the key in screenshots, notes or public posts.
2. Enter your niche and location
Write a focused query such as restaurants in Boston. Choose 10 matches for a small first run. Google Places may expand queries; Foursquare makes one search request.
3. Follow progress and review results
Wait for completion or cancel if needed. Review the final count and stop reason. A target is an upper bound, not a promise of that number of matches.
4. Filter and check details
For Foursquare, filter by available website, phone or social profile. Verify business relevance and contact details yourself before outreach. Save or share only where source permissions allow.
